When something changes on the screen in Jetpack Compose, Compose does not blindly rebuild and redraw the entire interface. It divides the work into three main phases:

• Composition — What should be displayed?

• Layout — How large should each element be, and where should it go?

• Drawing — What pixels should be rendered?
Understanding these phases makes many Compose concepts easier to reason about: recomposition, state reads, modifiers, unnecessary work, and even some apparently mysterious performance problems.
One terminology note before we begin: people sometimes call these the “three composition phases,” but composition is actually only the first phase. A more accurate name is the three phases of rendering in Compose.
❓Why Is Understanding These Phases Important?
Understanding these phases helps you predict how Compose will react when state changes. You can identify whether a change requires recomposition, a new layout calculation, or only redrawing some pixels.
It helps:

• Understand why recomposition happens

• Detect unnecessary recompositions

• Build smoother…
